    Easy Zuppa Toscana Recipe

    This Zuppa Toscana soup recipe is pure comfort in a bowl, made with Italian sausage, tender potatoes, kale, and crispy bacon in a rich, creamy broth. It’s easy to make at home in one pot and always a family favorite.

    This Zuppa Toscana (Tuscan soup) is rich, decadent, and so satisfying, but I think my favorite part is that anyone who eats it loves it. This cozy soup just has a way of bringing everyone together! It's ridiculously easy to make, even on a busy weeknight, which makes it a strong contender for your regular soup rotation.

    Serve it with my soft French bread or homemade focaccia to soak up that silky, creamy broth.

    Ingredients You'll Need

    • Bacon – Freshly cooked bacon adds smoky flavor and a crisp texture in every bite. For a shortcut, use cooked, crumbled bacon.
    • Italian sausage – Mild or spicy Italian sausage both work. I like mild for a family-friendly soup, then anyone who wants more heat can add crushed red pepper when serving.
    • Onion and garlic – These cook in the flavorful drippings left in the pot after browning the bacon and sausage.
    • Russet potatoes – You’ll need about 1 pound, or 4 cups diced. I peel them because the skins can loosen in the soup, but you can leave them on if you prefer. Other popular potato varieties will work too.
    • Chicken broth – Four cups create the base of the soup. Keep a little extra broth or water nearby in case you want more liquid as the potatoes cook.
    • Kale – Use any kale variety, including curly kale or Lacinato kale, also called Tuscan or dinosaur kale. Two tightly packed cups give you plenty of kale throughout the soup without overwhelming it. Add more if you love your greens.
    • Heavy cream – This gives Zuppa Toscana its rich, silky broth and holds up well to the gentle simmer at the end.
    • Salt and black pepper – I recommend starting with the amounts listed, then seasoning to taste. Bacon, sausage, and chicken broth can all vary quite a bit in saltiness.

    How To Make Zuppa Toscana Soup

    1. Cook the bacon and sausage. Cook the bacon in a 4.5-quart pot over medium heat until crisp, then transfer it to a paper-towel-lined plate. Leave 1–2 tablespoons of bacon grease in the pot. Brown the sausage in the drippings, then transfer it to a plate and set aside.

    2. Sauté the onion and garlic. Add the onion to the pot and cook until softened. Add the garlic and cook briefly, stirring as needed.

    3. Cook the potatoes. Add the potatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender. Add a little water or more broth if you want more liquid.

    4. Finish the soup. Return the sausage to the pot and stir in the kale, heavy cream, salt, and black pepper. Gently simmer for about 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve topped with plenty of crispy bacon.

    Recipe Tips for the Best Zuppa Toscana

    • Bacon shortcuts: Use pre-cooked crumbled bacon to save about 15 minutes. Or, cook raw bacon separately while the sausage browns in a little oil. Freshly cooked crispy bacon is the chef's kiss of this soup.
    • Potato prep: Dice the potatoes into ½-inch pieces so they cook evenly and quickly. To prep ahead, submerge the diced potatoes completely in water and refrigerate.
    • Don't overcook the potatoes: Once they're fork-tender, continue with the recipe without unnecessary simmering. They'll keep softening in the hot soup.
    • Kale options: Use curly kale or Lacinato kale, also called Tuscan or dinosaur kale. Use more than 2 cups if you love your greens.
    • Thicken the soup naturally: For a thicker broth, mash a few cooked potatoes in the pot.

    Recipe Variations

    • Make it spicy: Use hot Italian sausage instead of mild, or sprinkle crushed red pepper over individual servings for adjustable heat.
    • Try different potatoes: I'm using Russet potatoes in these photos, but Yukon Gold or red potatoes work too. Keep the pieces about the same size so they cook evenly.
    • Use spinach: Substitute fresh spinach for the kale. Stir it in just before serving since it wilts much faster than kale.
    • Add more kale: I use 2 tightly packed cups, but you can increase it to 4 cups if you like a greener, more veggie-packed soup.
    • Lighter creamy broth: For a lighter soup, replace some of the heavy cream with water. Add it with the chicken broth, then finish with less cream to taste.

    Easy Zuppa Toscana Soup Recipe

    This Zuppa Toscana soup recipe is pure comfort in a bowl, made with Italian sausage, tender potatoes, kale, and crispy bacon in a rich, creamy broth. It’s easy to make at home in one pot and always a family favorite.
    Prep TimePrep Time 15 minutes mins
    Cook TimeCook Time 30 minutes mins
    Total timeTotal time 45 minutes mins
    Yield 8 cups
    Author Traci
    5 from 50 votes

    Note about scaling

    When scaling, the light gray ingredient notes after the comma don’t change. Adjust as needed.

    Ingredients 

    • 8 ounces Bacon, coarsely chopped
    • 1 pound Italian Sausage (Mild or Spicy), casings removed, if any
    • 1 medium Onion, diced
    • 4 cloves Garlic, minced
    • 4 small Russet Potatoes, peeled and diced, about 1 pound or 4 cups
    • 4 cups Chicken Broth
    • 2 cups Kale, tightly packed, about 2 ounces
    • 1 cup Heavy Cream
    • ¼ teaspoon Salt, or to taste
    • ⅛ teaspoon Black Pepper, or to taste

    Instructions

    • Cook the bacon: Cook the BACON in a 4.5-quart pot over medium heat until crisp.
    • Drain the bacon: Transfer the BACON to a paper-towel-lined plate and set aside. Spoon out all but 1–2 tablespoons of bacon grease.
    • Brown the sausage: Add the ITALIAN SAUSAGE and break into crumbles. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Transfer to the same plate as the bacon and set aside.
      Note: Let the sausage cook undisturbed for a minute or two between stirring so it develops flavorful browned edges.
    • Sauté the aromatics: Add the ONION and cook for a few minutes, until softened. Add the GARLIC and cook briefly, stirring as needed.
    • Cook the potatoes: Add the POTATOES and CHICKEN BROTH. Increase the heat and bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are almost fork-tender.
    • Finish the soup: Return the SAUSAGE to the pot. Stir in the KALE, HEAVY CREAM, SALT, and BLACK PEPPER. Simmer gently for about 5 minutes.
    • Season and serve: Taste the soup and add more SALT if needed. Serve warm with crumbled BACON.
    • Storage and reheat: Cool completely and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Reheat gently using your preferred method until warmed through.

    Recipe Notes

    Recipe update: I revised and retested this recipe in Fall 2026, improving the cooking method and updating the ingredient amounts. It's even more lovable now!
    Bacon shortcuts: Use pre-cooked crumbled bacon to save about 15 minutes. Or, cook raw bacon separately while the sausage browns in a little oil. Freshly cooked crispy bacon is the chef's kiss of this soup.
    Potato prep: Dice the potatoes into ½-inch pieces so they cook evenly and quickly. To prep ahead, submerge the diced potatoes completely in water and refrigerate.
    Don't overcook the potatoes: Once they're fork-tender, continue with the recipe without unnecessary simmering. They'll keep softening in the hot soup.
    Kale options: Use curly kale or Lacinato kale, also called Tuscan or dinosaur kale. Use more than 2 cups if you love your greens.
    Thicken the soup naturally: For a thicker broth, mash a few cooked potatoes in the pot.
    ____________
    Pressure cooker instructions: Use Sauté mode to cook bacon until crisp; remove. Brown sausage; remove. Sauté onion and garlic in 1–2 tablespoons bacon grease. Add potatoes and chicken broth. Pressure cook on high for 5 minutes followed by a 10-minute natural pressure release, then release any remaining pressure. Stir in sausage, kale, heavy cream, salt, and black pepper. Use Sauté mode to warm through. Serve topped with bacon.

    Equipment

    • chef's knife
    • cutting board
    • measuring cups and spoons
    • 4.5-quart soup pot
    • slotted spoon
